source.title: A Scaling Transition Method from SGDM to SGD with 2ExpLR Strategy
source.authors: Kun Zeng; Jin-Lan Liu; Zhixia Jiang; Dongpo Xu

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, though some figure labels and references are flattened or garbled.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers on image-classification test accuracy and reports training accuracy, using its own TSGD method alongside plain SGD and adaptive optimizers.
record.gate_note: The optimizer comparisons in Tables 1–5 bear on V4. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected architecture as an intervention, batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Figure-only curves and cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: Tables 1–5 directly compare adaptive optimizers with the NSGD reference on held-out image-classification accuracy. These comparisons test V4, although comparator hyperparameters are default or empirical rather than systematically tuned.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: the authors propose a scaled transition from momentum SGD to plain SGD, combined with a decreasing learning rate, and report faster convergence and good generalization performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper's main intervention is a scaling transition from momentum SGD to plain SGD (TSGD); optimizer comparisons use the authors' experimental settings and optimal values, with default or empirical hyperparameters for the other methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy differs between experiments with and without StepLR; the paper also varies upper and lower learning rates and the transition factor γ, reporting that larger γ values have less ideal convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: TSGD achieves the highest reported test accuracy in all five tables and is reported to improve convergence speed and stability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transitioning from momentum SGD to plain SGD can improve optimization and held-out accuracy under the tested recipes.

record.problems: The tables report optimal values across the training process rather than a single matched endpoint; hyperparameters for comparison methods are described as default or empirical. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run results are reported, and the MNIST comparison has equal training accuracy across methods while the image-classification comparisons have markedly different training accuracies.
record.rows_left_out: No tabled test-accuracy results were omitted. Figure-only training curves and hyperparameter-sensitivity curves in Figures 2–17 were not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Generalization as width increases beyond interpolation.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.

Systematic learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; language benchmarks. The better-training-performance clause is demonstrated only in some comparisons.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All table values match the supplied text. They are best values during training, potentially selected at different iterations, rather than matched final checkpoints. Results use one shared seed and report no repeated-run uncertainty. The NSGD table label is not explicitly expanded, and the prose alternates between plain SGD and SGDM terminology. Schedule choice reverses several optimizer rankings. These findings qualify a conditional claim about what happens often; they do not establish its overall frequency across benchmarks. Figure-only results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and local connectivity.
Limited-tuning comparison in the cited benchmarks; broader tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, decoupled weight decay, and word-level language models.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.
